h: חַג הַפֶּסַח, מַאֲמָר ח׳ Pesach — Maamar Ches

p: בָּרוּךְ הַמָּקוֹם, בָּרוּךְ הוּא, בָּרוּךְ שֶׁנָּתַן תּוֹרָה לְעַמּוֹ יִשְׂרָאֵל.
"Blessed is the Omnipresent, blessed is He, blessed is He Who gave the Torah to His people Israel."
בָּזֶה מְרוּמָּז שְׁלֹשָׁה עִנְיָנִים שֶׁאֲנוּ מוֹדִים לְהַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא עֲלֵיהֶם,
In this are alluded three matters for which we thank the Holy One, blessed is He,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁמְּסַיֵּים: כְּנֶגֶד אַרְבָּעָה בָנִים דִּבְּרָה תוֹרָה.
as it concludes: "Corresponding to four sons the Torah spoke."
וְלִכְאוֹרָה יֵשׁ לְהָבִין בְּהָא דִּכְתִיב
Now ostensibly one must understand what is written
(שְׁמוֹת י"ב, כ"ו):
(Shemos 12:26):
וְהָיָה כִּי יֹאמְרוּ אֲלֵיכֶם בְּנֵיכֶם מָה הָעֲבֹדָה הַזֹּאת לָכֶם וְגוֹמֵר וַיִּקֹּד הָעָם וַיִּשְׁתַּחֲווּ,
"And it shall be when your children say to you, 'What is this service to you?' etc., and the people bowed their heads and prostrated themselves,"
וּפֵירֵשׁ רַשִׁ"י: עַל בְּשׂוֹרַת הַבָּנִים!
and Rashi explained: "[They prostrated themselves] over the tidings of having children!"
הֲלֹא זֶה הוּא שְׁאֵלַת בֶּן הָרָשָׁע—וּמַה זוֹ בְּשׂוֹרָה שֶׁיִּהְיֶה לָהֶם בָּנִים רְשָׁעִים?!
Surely this is the question of the wicked son—so what good tidings is it that they will have wicked children?!
וְגַם מַה זוֹ בְּשׂוֹרָה שֶׁיִּוָּלְדוּ בָּנִים?
And also, what good tidings is it that children will be born?
זֶה יִתָּכֵן לְאִישׁ פְּרָטִי הוּא בְּשׂוֹרָה שֶׁיִּוָּלֵד בָּנִים,
That would make sense for a private individual as good tidings that he will have children,
אֲבָל לְאוּמָּה שְׁלֵימָה הֲלוֹא עוֹלָם כְּמִנְהָגוֹ נוֹהֵג שֶׁנּוֹשְׂאִים נָשִׁים וּמוֹלִידִים בָּנִים!
but for an entire nation, surely the world follows its natural course that people marry and bear children!
אַךְ עִיקַּר הַבְּשׂוֹרָה הָיָה לָהֶם שֶׁאַף הַבָּנִים רְשָׁעִים שֶׁיִּוָּלְדוּ לָהֶם לֹא יִדָּחוּ מִכְּלַל יִשְׂרָאֵל לְעוֹלָם,
However, the essence of the good tidings to them was that even the wicked children born to them will never be cast out from the community of Israel,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁמּוּבָא בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ
as brought in the holy Zohar
(חֵלֶק א' צ"ג.):
כְּתִיב: וְעַמֵּךְ כֻּלָּם צַדִּיקִים, וְהָא כַּמָּה חַיָּיבִין אִית בְּהוּ בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל וְכוּלֵּי?
"It is written, 'And Your people are all righteous'—yet how many sinners are there among Israel, etc.?
אֶלָּא הָכִי תְּנָא וְכוּלֵּי:
Rather, thus it was taught, etc.:
וְכַד אִתְגְּזָרוּ עָאלוּ בְּהַאי חוּלָּקָא טָבָא דְּקוּדְשָׁא בְּרִיךְ הוּא, דִּכְתִיב
when they are circumcised, they enter into this good portion of the Holy One, blessed is He, as it is written
(מִשְׁלֵי י', כ"ה):
(Mishlei 10:25):
וְצַדִּיק יְסוֹד עוֹלָם
'And the righteous is the foundation of the world'
כֵּיוָן דְּעָאלוּ בְּהַאי חוּלָּקָא דְּצַדִּיק, וַדַּאי כֻּלָּם צַדִּיקִים וְגוֹמֵר לְעוֹלָם יִירְשׁוּ אָרֶץ.
once they have entered into this portion of Tzaddik, certainly 'all of them are righteous, etc., forever they shall inherit the land.'"
וְכֵן אִיתָא בַּגְּמָרָא
And so it is stated in the Gemara
(סַנְהֶדְרִין מ"ד.)
(Sanhedrin 44a)
בְּעָכָן:
regarding Achan:
אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁחָטָא יִשְׂרָאֵל הוּא;
"Even though he has sinned, he is still Israel"
אָסָא דְּקָאֵי בֵּינֵי חִילְפֵי, אָסָא שְׁמוֹ וְאָסָא קָרֵי לֵיהּ
a myrtle standing among thorns is still named myrtle and called myrtle
אַף שֶׁעָבַר עַל כָּל הַתּוֹרָה וּמָשַׁךְ בְּעָרְלָתוֹ שֶׁרָצָה שֶׁלֹּא יַכִּירוּ בוֹ שֶׁהוּא מָהוּל,
even though he transgressed the entire Torah and disguised his circumcision so that people would not recognize he was circumcised,
אַף עַל פִּי כֵן אָמַר לוֹ יְהוֹשֻׁעַ: יַעְכָּרְךָ ה' הַיּוֹם הַזֶּה
nevertheless Yehoshua said to him: "Hashem shall trouble you this day"
הַיּוֹם הַזֶּה אַתָּה עָכוּר, וְיֵשׁ לְךָ חֵלֶק לָעוֹלָם הַבָּא.
"this day you are troubled, yet you have a portion in the World to Come."
וְגַם אִיתָא בַּמִּשְׁנָה
And it is also stated in the Mishnah
(ibid. 90a):
שְׁלֹשָׁה מְלָכִים וְאַרְבָּעָה הֶדְיוֹטוֹת שֶׁאֵין לָהֶם חֵלֶק לָעוֹלָם הַבָּא,
"Three kings and four commoners have no portion in the World to Come,"
וּבַגְּמָרָא
and in the Gemara
(ibid. 104b):
דּוֹרְשֵׁי רְשׁוּמוֹת אָמְרוּ: כּוּלָּם בָּאִים לָעוֹלָם הַבָּא חוּץ מִבִּלְעָם.
"The interpreters of subtle allusions (Dorshei Reshumos) said: All of them enter the World to Come except for Bilam."
דּוֹרְשֵׁי רְשׁוּמוֹת הַיְינוּ שֶׁמַּשִּׂיגִים הַרְגָּשָׁה לְמַעְלָה מִשֵּׂכֶל אֱנוֹשִׁי, וְהוּא רַק כְּמוֹ רוֹשֶׁם
Dorshei Reshumos are those who attain a perception above human intellect, which is like a mere trace
דְּאַנְשֵׁי כְּנֶסֶת הַגְּדוֹלָה אָמְרוּ עֲלֵיהֶם שֶׁאֵין לָהֶם חֵלֶק לָעוֹלָם הַבָּא עַל פִּי שֵׂכֶל הַשָּׂגַת אֱנוֹשִׁי,
for the Men of the Great Assembly ruled that they have no portion in the World to Come according to the grasp of human intellect,
וְרַק הַדּוֹרְשֵׁי רְשׁוּמוֹת אָמְרוּ שֶׁיֵּשׁ לָהֶם חֵלֶק לָעוֹלָם הַבָּא מֵחֲמַת שֶׁהֵם מִזֶּרַע יִשְׂרָאֵל,
whereas the Dorshei Reshumos said they do have a portion in the World to Come because they are of the seed of Israel,
וְאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁחָטָא יִשְׂרָאֵל הוּא וְלֹא יִדַּח מִמֶּנּוּ נִדָּח.
and even though he has sinned he is still Israel, "and none shall be cast out from Him."
וְעַל הַבְּשׂוֹרָה הַזּוֹ הָיוּ שְׂמֵחִים, וְעַל זֶה נֶאֱמַר: וַיִּקֹּד הָעָם וַיִּשְׁתַּחֲווּ
And over this good tidings they rejoiced, and concerning this it is said: "And the people bowed their heads and prostrated themselves"
עַל בְּשׂוֹרַת הַזֶּרַע, שֶׁהוּבְטַח לָהֶם שֶׁיִּהְיֶה לְזַרְעָם קְדוּשַּׁת יִשְׂרָאֵל לְעוֹלָם.
over the tidings of offspring, that they were promised their descendants would retain the holiness of Israel forever.
וְהִנֵּה "בָּרוּךְ הַמָּקוֹם" מְרַמֵּז לְבֵן חָכָם,
Now "Blessed is the Omnipresent (HaMakom)" alludes to the wise son,
שֶׁהוּא מַשְׂכִּיל בַּתּוֹרָה וְיֵשׁ לוֹ הַכָּרָה בִּכְבוֹד מַלְכוּתוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ שְׁמוֹ,
who is wise in Torah and possesses recognition of the glory of His kingship, blessed be His Name
וְעַל זֶה מְרַמֵּז תֵּיבַת "הַמָּקוֹם"
and to this the word "HaMakom" alludes
וְשׁוֹאֵל בְּדֶרֶךְ חָכְמָה שֶׁרוֹצֶה לְהַשִּׂיג טַעַם וְחַיּוּת מִקְּדוּשַּׁת מִצְווֹת הַתּוֹרָה,
and he asks in a wise manner, desiring to grasp the flavor and vitality of the holiness of the Torah's mitzvos;
וְעַל זֶה בָּא הַתְּשׁוּבָה: אֵין מַפְטִירִין אַחַר הַפֶּסַח אֲפִיקוֹמָן
and to this comes the answer: "We do not conclude after the Pesach offering with afikoman"
הַיְינוּ שֶׁתַּכְנִיס בּוֹ חַיּוּת הַדִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה שֶׁלֹּא תָּפוּג טַעְמוֹ מִמֶּנּוּ;
meaning that you should instill in him the vitality of words of Torah so its flavor never leaves his palate;
וּ"בָּרוּךְ הַמָּקוֹם" הַיְינוּ שֶׁיֵּשׁ לָנוּ הַשָּׂגָה בְּשֵׂכֶל אֱנוֹשִׁי בְּטַעַם וְחַיּוּת כְּבוֹד קְדוּשָּׁתוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ שְׁמוֹ.
and "Blessed is HaMakom" means that we have a grasp within human intellect of the flavor and vitality of the glory of His holiness, blessed be His Name.
וְעַל שְׁאֵלַת בֶּן הָרָשָׁע בָּא הַתְּשׁוּבָה: אִילּוּ הָיָה שָׁם לֹא הָיָה נִגְאָל,
And to the question of the wicked son comes the answer: "Had he been there, he would not have been redeemed,"
אֲבָל אַחַר שֶׁגָּאַל אוֹתָנוּ ה' יִתְבָּרַךְ וְעָשָׂה אוֹתָנוּ לְאוּמָּה יִשְׂרְאֵלִית,
but now that Hashem, may He be blessed, has redeemed us and made us into the Israelite nation,
מֵעַתָּה כֵּיוָן שֶׁגַּם הוּא נוֹלַד מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל וְנִימּוֹל לִשְׁמוֹנָה,
henceforth, since he too was born of Israel and circumcised on the eighth day,
לֹא יוֹעִיל לוֹ רִשְׁעָתוֹ לְהוֹצִיא עַצְמוֹ מִכְּלַל יִשְׂרָאֵל, אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁעָשָׂה תּוֹעֵבוֹת,
his wickedness will not avail to remove him from the community of Israel, even if he committed abominations,
וְאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁחָטָא יִשְׂרָאֵל הוּא וְיִהְיֶה לוֹ תִּיקּוּן גַּם עַל מַעֲשָׂיו;
and even though he has sinned he is still Israel, and there will be rectification for his deeds as well;
וְעַל זֶה מְרַמֵּז תֵּיבַת "בָּרוּךְ הוּא" בִּלְשׁוֹן נִסְתָּר,
and to this the phrase "Blessed is He (Hu)" in the third-person hidden form alludes,
שֶׁתֵּיבַת "הוּא" מְרַמֵּז עַל הֶעָתִיד שֶׁנֶּעְלָם מִשֵּׂכֶל אֱנוֹשִׁי,
for the word "Hu" alludes to the future that is concealed from human intellect,
כִּי אֵין שׁוּם הַשָּׂגָה בְּשִׂכְלֵנוּ אֵיךְ יוּכַל הָרָשָׁע לָבוֹא לִידֵי תִּיקּוּן,
since there is no grasp in our intellect of how the wicked person can come to rectification,
אֲבָל ה' יִתְבָּרַךְ שֶׁהוּא לְמַעְלָה מֵהַשָּׂגָתֵינוּ הִבְטִיחָנוּ שֶׁלֹּא יִדַּח מִמֶּנּוּ נִדָּח.
but Hashem, may He be blessed, Who is beyond our grasp, promised us that "none shall be cast out from Him."
וְעַל עִנְיַן הַתָּם מְרַמֵּז תֵּיבַת "בָּרוּךְ שֶׁנָּתַן תּוֹרָה לְעַמּוֹ יִשְׂרָאֵל",
And to the matter of the simple son alludes the phrase "Blessed is He Who gave the Torah to His people Israel,"
כִּי עַל יְדֵי הַדִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה תּוּכַל לְהַכְנִיס גַּם בְּהַתָּם דַּעַת לִהְיוֹת לוֹ הַשָּׂגָה קְצָת בִּקְדוּשָּׁתוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ שְׁמוֹ.
for through words of Torah you can instill knowledge even into the simple son so that he attains some grasp of His holiness, blessed be His Name.
וְעַל עִנְיַן שֶׁאֵינוֹ יוֹדֵעַ לִשְׁאוֹל מְרַמֵּז גַּם כֵּן תֵּיבַת "בָּרוּךְ הוּא",
And to the matter of the one who does not know how to ask also alludes the phrase "Blessed is He,"
שֶׁלָּזֶה גַּם כֵּן אֵין הַשָּׂגַת שֵׂכֶל אֱנוֹשִׁי לְהַשִּׂיג אֵיזֶה צַד קְדוּשַּׁת יִשְׂרָאֵל בְּנֶפֶשׁ בּוּר שֶׁלְּגַמְרֵי אֵין בּוֹ דַּעַת לִשְׁאוֹל וְאֵין לוֹ שׁוּם הַרְגָּשָׁה בִּקְדוּשָּׁתוֹ,
for here too human intellect cannot grasp what aspect of Israel's holiness exists in an unlearned soul who completely lacks the knowledge to ask and has no feeling for His holiness,

וְרַק מִצַּד ה' יִתְבָּרַךְ שֶׁהוּא לְמַעְלָה מֵהַשָּׂגַת שֵׂכֶל אֱנוֹשִׁי הִבְטִיחָנוּ שֶׁגַּם בַּנְּפָשׁוֹת הָהֵם גַּם כֵּן מִכְּלַל יִשְׂרָאֵל יֵחָשְׁבוּ וְנוּכַל גַּם בְּנַפְשָׁם לְהַכְנִיס קְדוּשָּׁה

and solely from the side of Hashem, may He be blessed, Who is beyond human intellectual grasp, He promised us that even those souls are counted within the community of Israel and we can instill holiness into their souls as well
"וְאַתְּ פְּתַח לוֹ", כִּי יֵשׁ בּוֹ גַּם כֵּן קְדוּשַּׁת יִשְׂרָאֵל.
"and you open for him," because he too possesses the holiness of Israel.

footnotes.heAnchorPrefix: אַךְ עִיקַּר הַבְּשׂוֹרָה הָיָה לָהֶם שֶׁאַף הַבָּנִים רְשָׁעִים שֶׁיִּוָּלְדוּ לָהֶם לֹא יִדָּחוּ מִכְּלַל יִשְׂרָאֵל לְעוֹלָם,

paragraphs.text: Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Nitzavim 6 — “Rashi explained: over the tidings of children. It was said to all Israel; what tidings is that? But since it said before, ‘And it shall be when your children say to you, What is this service to you,’ which is the question of the wicked son, and yet it is written ‘vehayah,’ an expression of joy, it means that even over a wicked son there is joy. So with Chizkiyahu, who refrained from having children because he saw Menashe would come from him, for from Menashe came the line of Mashiach; and even of Menashe himself the Dorshei Reshumos said he has a portion in the World to Come.” Connection: The same reading of Rashi, adding the case of Menashe: the line of redemption itself can come through the wicked son.

rich.text: — “Rashi explained: over the tidings of children. It was said to all Israel; what tidings is that? But since it said before, ‘And it shall be when your children say to you, What is this service to you,’ which is the question of the wicked son, and yet it is written ‘vehayah,’ an expression of joy, it means that even over a wicked son there is joy. So with Chizkiyahu, who refrained from having children because he saw Menashe would come from him, for from Menashe came the line of Mashiach; and even of Menashe himself the Dorshei Reshumos said he has a portion in the World to Come.” Connection: The same reading of Rashi, adding the case of Menashe: the line of redemption itself can come through the wicked son.

paragraphs.text: Zohar I 93a (Lech Lecha) — "R. Abba opened: 'Your people are all righteous' (Yeshayahu 60:21). Why is it written so — are all Israel righteous? There are so many wicked in Israel, so many sinners who transgress the commandments of the Torah!" The answer that follows: whoever is circumcised and enters the portion of the Tzaddik is called righteous.

paragraphs.text: Parallel: Sod Yesharim, First Night of Pesach 8 — “‘Blessed is He’ corresponds to the question of the wicked son, for the hidden world is called ‘Hu’ and the lower world is called ‘Atah.’ The wicked son argues that since God’s choice of Israel is beyond this world’s intellect, there is no ‘Atah’ here, that is, no human service, and all is still ‘Hu.’ The one who does not know how to ask also has ‘Blessed is He,’ but the wicked son does not desire service, and will truly remain in the aspect of ‘Hu’ until his own grasp is wholly nullified, whereas the one who does not know how to ask, if told that God desires service, will be ready to listen.” Connection: The same assignment of “Blessed is He” to both sons; Sod Yesharim adds the Hu–Atah distinction and what separates them.
